purpose: The field-shaped button in a top bar that opens search: a magnifier, a muted label (`Search` by default) and the keycap of the shortcut that opens the same palette (`⌘K` on macOS, `Ctrl K` elsewhere, drawn by `Kbd`). It looks like an input so the bar reads "you can search here", but it is one `<button>` that emits `click`; the consumer opens `Command` (or its own search) from it. With `collapsible` it folds to the magnifier alone inside a narrow container, so one element serves the wide and the narrow bar.
useWhen: The search entry of a console, demo or docs top bar (`GlobalHeader` end region) that opens the `Command` palette or a search dialog.
Anywhere a shortcut-backed launcher should look like a field without being one.
avoidWhen: To type a query in place (filter a list, search a table) → use `Input` with a search icon, `PropertyFilter`, or the `Table` search part.
For the palette itself → use `Command`; this only opens it.
For an icon-only toolbar action that is not search → use `IconButton`.
related: Command` — the palette this button opens; it owns the global ⌘K / Ctrl+K listener and `v-model:open`.
Kbd` — draws the keycap with the OS-aware modifier glyph.
IconButton` — the shape the trigger folds to when `collapsible` and the container is narrow.
GlobalHeader` — the bar it sits in, usually in `GlobalHeader.Right`.
bestPractices: Wire `@click` to the same state the shortcut opens (`<Command v-model:open="open">`), so the button and ⌘K never disagree.
Keep `shortcut` equal to the key the `Command` root listens for (`K`), or clear it (`shortcut=""`) when no shortcut exists.
With `collapsible`, put the bar inside an `@container` (the header blocks do); the trigger folds below the container's `2xl` size and without a container it stays folded.
Name the target in the label when the scope is narrow (`Search docs`); the label is also the accessible name.
